title: Water-gas shift reference family
objective: Optional literature-backed thermal-catalyst family for water-gas-shift screening. These candidates compare conventional Cu/ZnO low-temperature practice with newer oxide-interface and noble-metal routes used for cleaner hydrogen generation.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: Balance catalyst cost, evidence quality, route maturity, and performance.

cost-first.label: Cost-first
cost-first.description: Bias ranking toward catalyst cost while preserving route and evidence guardrails.

evidence-first.label: Evidence-first
evidence-first.description: Reward transparent inputs and more defensible preparation routes.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2017
citations.note: Cu-facet study identifying Cu(100)-suboxide interfaces as highly active sites for low-temperature water-gas shift.

citations.label: Nature 2021
citations.note: Crowded Pt on alpha-MoC route showing very high low-temperature WGS activity and stability.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2021
citations.note: Dynamic active-site study of Pt/CeO2 under WGS conditions, useful for route-confidence and site-stability framing.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2023
citations.note: CeO2-x/CoO1-x/Co dual-interface route boosting WGS reactivity without moving fully to a PGM basis.

citations.label: Nature Communications 2025
citations.note: Study quantifying how platinum electronic and geometric effects control WGS activity.

citations.label: Science 2003
citations.note: Fu, Saltsburg & Flytzani-Stephanopoulos: landmark identification of nonmetallic Au and Pt species on ceria as the active phase in low-temperature WGS.

citations.label: Catalysis Communications 2003
citations.note: Luengnaruemitchai, Osuwan & Gulari: comparative low-temperature WGS over Pt/CeO2, Au/CeO2, and Au/Fe2O3.

citations.label: Science 2010
citations.note: Zhai, Pierre et al.: alkali-stabilized Pt-OHx species as the catalytically active phase for low-temperature WGS, refining the picture of Pt/oxide interfacial sites.

citations.label: Catalysis Reviews 2009
citations.note: Standard industrial water-gas shift review covering the Fe-Cr high-temperature shift class.

citations.label: ACS Catalysis 2016
citations.note: Review of iron-based high-temperature WGS catalysts: hematite-to-magnetite activation, Cr2O3 textural stabilization, Cu promotion, 350-450 C window.

citations.label: Applied Petrochemical Research 2019
citations.note: Source of the 88/9/2.6 wt% Fe2O3/Cr2O3/CuO pellet composition and the 310-460 C operating window.

citations.label: ACS Catalysis 2016
citations.note: Cr and Cu promotion mechanisms of iron-oxide HT-WGS catalysts with the ammonia-assisted co-precipitation preparation.

route_templates.name: Cu-ZnO low-temperature WGS route
route_templates.route_note: Most transferable screening basis for industrial low-temperature WGS catalyst manufacture.

route_templates.name: Co-CeO2 interfacial WGS route
route_templates.route_note: Promising non-noble WGS route, but it depends on tighter oxide-interface control than the Cu/ZnO baseline.

route_templates.name: Pt-CeO2 premium WGS route
route_templates.route_note: High-performance low-temperature WGS route used when hydrogen purity and colder operation justify a PGM premium.

route_templates.name: Fe-Cr-Cu co-precipitation with pelletizing
synthesis: Ammonia-assisted co-precipitation of the mixed hydroxides
Aging and washing of the precipitate
postprocess: Calcination near 400 C to the hematite phase
quality_gates: Shift-activity spot test after in-service magnetite activation
route_templates.route_note: One of the oldest continuously practiced industrial catalyst manufacturing chains; hematite converts to the active magnetite in service, so no reduction step is charged.

candidates.title: Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 baseline
candidates.summary: Industrial low-temperature WGS basis using copper-zinc oxide with alumina support or binder.
decision_notes: Best fit when the goal is a defensible industrial WGS screening anchor with transparent copper exposure.
Route maturity is highest in the family even if the absolute activity ceiling is lower than Pt-led routes.

pricing.note: Live copper feed with precursor conversion markup.
USGS MCS 2026 North American SHG zinc, 2025e $1.49/lb, x 0.803 Zn mass fraction of ZnO = $1.20/lb contained-metal floor; oxide conversion cost not included.
2025 USGS alumina import value used as a bulk support or binder proxy.

candidates.title: Co-CeO2 interface route
candidates.summary: Cobalt-ceria route that targets stronger low-temperature WGS reactivity through oxide-interface engineering.
decision_notes: Strong option when non-noble pricing matters but a plain Cu/ZnO basis is too conservative on low-temperature performance.
The route premium comes from interfacial discipline and ceria handling rather than raw-metal scarcity.

pricing.note: Live cobalt feed with precursor conversion markup.
2025 USGS cerium-oxide price used as a bulk oxygen-storage support proxy.

candidates.title: Pt/CeO2 premium
candidates.summary: Pt/CeO2 route for WGS when colder hydrogen-cleanup duty justifies a noble-metal premium.
decision_notes: Performance leader for colder WGS duty, but economics are directly tied to Pt exposure.
Use as a premium benchmark for hydrogen-polishing scenarios rather than a default cost anchor.

pricing.note: Live Pt feed with mild precursor markup for low-loading deposition.
2025 USGS cerium-oxide price used as a bulk support proxy.

candidates.title: Fe2O3-Cr2O3(-CuO) high-temperature shift
candidates.summary: Pelletized 88/9/2.6 wt% Fe2O3/Cr2O3/CuO runs the high-temperature shift at 310-460 C; hematite activates to magnetite in service with chromia as the sintering stabilizer and copper as the chemical promoter.
decision_notes: The upstream stage of the industrial two-stage shift: cheapest metals in the family and a fully de-risked route, equilibrium-limited at its higher operating temperature.
Hexavalent-chromium handling during manufacture is a compliance cost outside this screen; noted, not priced.

pricing.note: Contained-Fe cost from bulk synthetic black iron oxide (ICIS 2006, $0.94/lb, CatCost library), ChemPPI-escalated. The scrap-iron market feed understates precursor chemistry ~40x, so Fe components price on a precursor basis.

pricing.evidence_label: UN Comtrade chromium-oxide import unit value
pricing.note: 2024 U.S. imports of HS 281990 (chromium oxides and hydroxides excl. trioxide): $16.45M / 2.91M kg = $5.66/kg CIF. Chromia is the documented textural stabilizer of the HTS formulation, carried in the support role.
Contained-copper basis of the 2.6 wt% CuO promoter with a mild precursor conversion markup.
